title: Derived tensor and Tor under normalized coefficient encoding
statement: For a finite discrete commutative ring A, a scheme T, and any normalized Encoding e supplied by [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding], the actual termwise fixed-scalar derived equivalence admits a strong monoidal structure. For every internal derived object K and every ordered interval a <= b, its generic Tor-amplitude condition is equivalent both to HasProEtaleTorAmplitude for the ordinary section-module image and to generic Tor-amplitude for the fixed scalar image. These are the existing derived tensors and all degree-zero test modules, not a newly transferred tensor structure.

proof.text: Equip the existing section-action equivalence with its strong monoidal structure using the tensor and unit isomorphisms, naturality, associator and unitor equations of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Compose with restriction along the specified ring-sheaf isomorphism using [lem-sfb-ring-isomorphism-tensor-transport]. The recorded ordinary_functor equality identifies this composite with the given ordinary equivalence. Restriction to constant sections is strong monoidal by [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-restriction-tensor]; the recorded fixed_functor equality identifies the actual fixed equivalence.

Compose the two strong monoidal equivalences and equip its inverse with the canonical adjoint monoidal structure. Apply [new-lem-kun-exact-monoidal-equivalence-derived] to its adjunction. This supplies a strong monoidal structure on its actual termwise extension, exactly fixedDerived, without transferring or redefining either native derived tensor.

For the ordinary module category identify the acyclic-tensor K-flat predicate with the quasi-isomorphism K-flat predicate by descending to the homotopy category and applying the acyclic criterion and symmetry. For every resolution P -> L representing K, [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] identifies Q(P tensor M[0]) with K tensor^L M[0]. The generic Tor predicate therefore implies the resolution predicate for every representative and resolution. Conversely choose a flat-term K-flat resolution by [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution] and use the same comparison to recover every degree-zero tensor test. The supplied inequality provides the ordered-interval conjunct.

An exact monoidal equivalence preserves flat objects. Apply the source library theorem DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_obj_iff to the ordinary equivalence and to the composite fixed equivalence. Compose the former equivalence of predicates with the resolution comparison in the preceding step; the latter gives the fixed-scalar assertion directly. These results have unrestricted derived objects, every degree-zero test module, and the specified integers; no constructibility or boundedness assumption is used.

lean.statement:
theorem encoding_tensor_tor [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (e : Encoding A T) :
    Nonempty (e.fixedDerived.functor.Monoidal) ∧
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b →
      (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔
        Scheme.HasProEtaleTorAmplitude T A (e.ordinaryDerived.functor.obj K) a b)) ∧
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b →
      (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔ DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b
        (e.fixedDerived.functor.obj K)))
